items.title: 61521_David Albert Francis oral history interview
items.q: Earl Hines played in Miami... Hartley Toots was going to have a new drummer

ctx.x: So, anyway, when all of the other boys was able to have, like four and five suits of clothes, I had a suit, period, that I wore to church. And the rest of that money, my mother took it, and paid her bills with it and played the numbers, which I detest -- to this day, I don't play numbers to this day, because of that. And my mother would spend up all my money playing numbers.

But, anyway, I stayed with George Kelly's band until around 1938. I'll never forget -- I think it was May 2nd or something like that, in 1938, and Earl Hines played in Miami, and Hartley Toots was going to have a new drummer; they were going to have a change in drummers, so I went to Mr. Rivers who owned the band -- Bill Rivers owned the band, see. Because at that time, in the band, there was Cat Anderson in that band at that time, in 1938.

items.title: 61521_David Albert Francis oral history interview
items.q: Louis Armstrong had Jack Teagarden T. Garden and Aurell Shore, and Earl Hines Arvell Shaw, was the piano player.

ctx.x: And, later on, when I came to New York, whenever he was in town, we used to hang out together every now and then, and I will never forget the time that I was out in California, and he had his own group at a club there, I think the club was called The Last Word, that was where I first saw Allen Eager -- Allen Eager was playing out there at the time.

And Sid and I used to hang out there, because at that time, he was doing very well for himself; I mean, as a leader. Then I got the pleasure of being with him again in at Wildwood, New Jersey when he was with Louis Armstrong. Louis Armstrong had Jack Teagarden T.
